ggchord.value: A ggchord object (inherits from ggplot) to which geom_* layers can be added with +

Supply one complete reference at plot level or declare it with a complete explicit `geom_seq(data = ...)` table. With a plot-level reference, a backbone may reuse all or a consistent subset of it. Without one, repeated backbone declarations must describe the same complete reference. The reference is resolved before drawing.

Observation layers use their own data or inherit the plot-level data. A reference supplied only through a backbone does not become the plot data. Inherited mappings are evaluated in each layer's data. Use `layout_sequences(order = ...)` to change the default reference order. The default coordinate projection is Chord.

Ordinary visual scales train together across layers by aesthetic, following ggplot2. Layer IDs identify the layers for references and export. Use `scale_for()` to train a scale on selected layers or tracks, and `scales_ggchord()` to use the traditional palettes.

shape_feature.intro: Build a custom outline from the prototype or adjust the parts of a preset for a layer or a shape scale.
shape_feature.value: An annotation shape specification for `shape` or `scale_shape_manual()`.
shape_feature.details:
Start with `shape_feature("prototype")` for a flat-ended block. Set the outline with `body_shape`, `head_shape` and `tail_shape`. A preset fixes the outline and lets you adjust its active dimensions and paint. The visible interval sets the total length. The body fills the space between the ends. On directional shapes, the strand determines the head and tail. Legend keys show a representative sample of the same profile.

`arrow` has a shouldered triangular head. `arrow_flush` uses the body width at the head base. `arrow_triangle` uses the full span. `arrow_arc` pairs a thin body with a triangular head. `chevron` pairs a triangular head with a notched tail. `capped_line` has a thin body with two caps. Choose `body_shape = "line"`, `head_shape = "cap"` and `tail_shape = "cap"` to build the same profile from the prototype.

Use `body_shape = "line"` and `head_shape = "circle"` for a lollipop; use `body_shape = "none"` with a circle or diamond head for a point or diamond. A tick or cut body with flat ends gives a normal stroke. For `arrow_flush`, a triangular head with the same width as its block body yields the flush profile.

A flat-ended block also works at a site or a cut boundary. The same specification spans the visible interval, draws a square centred at `pos`, or draws a square on the corresponding side of each known cut boundary. A cut without known boundaries produces no square. The cut legend shows a representative staggered pair. The site and cut layers use their documented glyphs.

The same lollipop specification places its stem at the visible interval or segment midpoint, at the recorded site `pos`, or at each known cut boundary. Interval stems connect the backbone to the feature track. At a site or cut boundary, the stem extends 1.5 times the layer size. The circle and diamond follow the same anchor rules for their centres. An interval tick marks the visible midpoint; a site tick marks `pos`.

Each part can supply its own fill and outline. A fixed or mapped layer `fill` and `colour` overrides its own channel across all parts. Explicit `NA` hides the corresponding channel. The part fills share an exterior outline, which can have a different colour on each part.

geom_seq.intro: Draw the reference paths that features and links follow. Use `geom_seq()` for the basic backbone and choose a single line, double line or filled band as needed. Use `geom_seq_arrow()` to show the displayed orientation at a glance. It draws a single line with a closed 2 mm arrowhead by default.

arguments.data: With `NULL` (the default), use the reference registered by [`ggchord()`](ggchord.html#api-ggchord) or another backbone layer. Supply a reference table or a function that selects rows from the registered reference.
arguments.geometry: Only in `geom_seq()`. With `"auto"`, use a double path in [`coord_circular()`](coord_circular.html#api-coord_circular) and a single line in other supported projections. Set `"line"`, `"double"` or `"band"` explicitly when the backbone style matters.
arguments.thickness: Only in `geom_seq()`, for a double path or a band. Positive distance in millimetres or absolute grid units (default 1 mm). For double lines it is the separation between paths. For bands it is the band width. Use a vector named by `accver` to vary it by sequence. A single line uses the `linewidth` aesthetic.
arguments.stat: Both functions require an identity Stat (default `"identity"`).
arguments.position: Use the identity Position (default) or [`position_offset()`](position_offset.html#api-position_offset) to displace the backbone.
Named styles and layer parameters such as `colour`, `linewidth` and `linetype`. A band also accepts `fill`. For a directional line, use `colour` for both the path and arrowhead.
arguments.arrow: An explicit argument to `geom_seq_arrow()`. Supply a `grid::arrow()` specification or use `NULL` for a plain line. The arrow follows the reference orientation shown by [`layout_sequences()`](layout_sequences.html#parameter-orientation). For explicit control on the basic backbone, pass `arrow` through `...` with `geom_seq(geometry = "line")`.

geom_seq.roles: The reference table defines sequence identity and length through `accver` and `length`. It can also declare `sequence_unit` and `topology`. Map visual properties with `aes()`: both functions take `colour`, `linewidth`, `linetype` and `alpha`. To map `fill`, set `geometry = "band"` in `geom_seq()`.
geom_seq.details: Both functions return a ggplot2 layer. A complete table supplied to a backbone can establish the reference in an otherwise empty `ggchord()` plot. Once the reference is registered, later backbone layers can select a subset or draw it with independent styling. A conflicting sequence definition or an unknown reference ID raises an error.

Each selected display instance can get its own label. Text aesthetics include `colour`, `size`, `family`, `fontface`, `angle` and `alpha`.

geom_feature.intro: Draw sequence annotations with `geom_feature()`. Use `geom_gene()`, `geom_primer()`, `geom_seq_region()`, `geom_site()` and `geom_restriction_site()` for marks with specialized defaults.

arguments.shape: Use a preset name or [`shape_feature()`](#api-shape_feature) specification. Map either with `aes(shape = category)` and `scale_shape_manual()`.
arguments.thickness: Physical thickness normal to the path, 2 mm by default. Supply a number in millimetres, an absolute grid unit or values selected by reference or strand. In circular maps this sets the shaft thickness for the arrow shapes. Set the symbol size with `size` in `geom_site()` or `thickness` in `geom_feature()`.
arguments.position: `geom_gene()` defaults to [`position_strand()`](position_strand.html#api-position_strand). The primer and region shortcuts use [`position_offset(0)`](position_offset.html#api-position_offset). The general feature, site and cut entries default to identity.
arguments.alpha: Explicit in `geom_seq_region()`, which defaults to 0.25. Set or map transparency to override that default.
Named visual styles and parameters for the selected Stat. Set arrow dimensions with [`shape_feature()`](#api-shape_feature).
arguments.stat: A compatible ggplot2 Stat or its name. The default uses the supplied records.

geom_feature.roles: Intervals use one-based inclusive `start` and `end`; directional marks use the source `strand`. Sites use one-based `pos`. Cuts retain `pos` as the residue anchor and use `cut_top` and `cut_bottom` for interbase coordinates. A supplied `entity_id` or an appropriate `feature_id` or `site_id` can identify a record across layers.
geom_feature.details:
| Entry point | Supported shapes |
| --- | --- |
| `geom_feature(location = "interval")`, `geom_gene()`, `geom_primer()` and `geom_seq_region()` | `block`, `arrow`, `arrow_flush`, `arrow_triangle`, `capped_line`, `arrow_arc`, `chevron`, `diamond`, `point`, `tick`, `lollipop`. Their respective defaults are `block`, `arrow_flush`, `arrow_arc` and `block`. |
| `geom_feature(location = "site")` and `geom_site()` | `tick` (default), `point`, `diamond`, `block`, `lollipop`. |
| `geom_feature(location = "cut")` and `geom_restriction_site()` | `cut` (default), `block`, `point`, `diamond`, `lollipop`. |

Use all interval shapes in [collinear coordinates](coord_collinear.html#api-coord_collinear) and [circular coordinates](coord_circular.html#api-coord_circular). Use `aes(shape = category)` with `scale_shape_manual(values = c(...))` to assign a shape to each category. Supply a fixed `shape` to use one glyph throughout the layer.

| Interval shape | Appearance and use |
| --- | --- |
| `"block"` | Default interval mark. A filled band drawn along the full interval. |
| `"arrow"` | Filled band with a directional head. |
| `"arrow_flush"` | Directional band with head base and shaft equally wide. |
| `"arrow_triangle"` | Wedge spanning the entire directional interval. |
| `"diamond"` | Diamond centred on the interval. |
| `"capped_line"` | Thin stroke with a cap inside each end. Set or map `colour` for the stroke and both caps. |
| `"arrow_arc"` | Slender directional stroke that follows the reference path. A standalone legend shows a straight sample of its outline. |
| `"chevron"` | Pointed band with a notched tail. |
| `"lollipop"` | Round head at the midpoint of the displayed interval or visible segment, with a stem to the reference backbone. |
| `"point"` | Circle centred on the visible interval. |
| `"tick"` | Short normal stroke at the visible interval midpoint. |

Start with `shape_feature("prototype")` for a flat-ended block. Set the outline with `body_shape`, `head_shape` and `tail_shape`. A preset fixes the outline and lets you adjust its active dimensions and paint. The visible interval sets the total length. The body fills the space between the ends. On directional shapes, the strand determines the head and tail. Legend keys show a representative sample of the same profile.

`arrow` has a shouldered triangular head. `arrow_flush` uses the body width at the head base. `arrow_triangle` uses the full span. `arrow_arc` pairs a thin body with a triangular head. `chevron` pairs a triangular head with a notched tail. `capped_line` has a thin body with two caps. Choose `body_shape = "line"`, `head_shape = "cap"` and `tail_shape = "cap"` to build the same profile from the prototype. Use `body_shape = "line"` and `head_shape = "circle"` for a lollipop; use `body_shape = "none"` with a circle or diamond head for a point or diamond. A tick or cut body with flat ends gives a normal stroke. For `arrow_flush`, a triangular head with the same width as its block body yields the flush profile.

A flat-ended block also works at a site or a cut boundary. The same specification spans the visible interval, draws a square centred at `pos`, or draws a square on the corresponding side of each known cut boundary. A cut without known boundaries produces no square. The cut legend shows a representative staggered pair. The site and cut layers use their documented glyphs.

Each part can supply its own fill and outline. A fixed or mapped layer `fill` and `colour` overrides its own channel across all parts. Explicit `NA` hides the corresponding channel. The part fills share an exterior outline, which can have a different colour on each part.

The same lollipop specification places its stem at the visible interval or segment midpoint, at the recorded site `pos`, or at each known cut boundary. Interval stems connect the backbone to the feature track. At a site or cut boundary, the stem extends 1.5 times the layer size. The circle and diamond follow the same anchor rules for their centres. An interval tick marks the visible midpoint; a site tick marks `pos`.

The `cut` preset draws a separate stroke at each known interbase boundary. The top stroke extends in the positive normal direction and the bottom stroke in the negative direction. Cut legend keys pair the upper-left and lower-right marks. Use `block` for a square on each boundary’s side, `point` or `diamond` for a glyph centred on the boundary, or `lollipop` for a stem and head facing outward. When both boundaries are missing, `cut` draws a tick at `pos` or reports an error according to `unknown_cut`. The other cut shapes omit the mark.

Use `"+"`, `"-"`, `"+/-"` or `"."` for strand. A `"+/-"` interval can draw two arrowheads while retaining one source identity. Legend keys summarise the glyph at a standard size. Read the actual length, direction and placement from the plotted interval. The [annotation label family](geom_feature_label.html#api-geom_feature_label) follows the displayed anchors.

geom_feature_label.intro: Use `geom_feature_label()` for interval, site or cut annotations. The gene, primer and site shortcuts select their respective kinds of targets. Choose a fixed or repelling text layout on any of these layers.

arguments.data: With a bound anchor and `data = NULL`, read the target entities after their Stat. To label an explicit subset, name the target in `anchor_layer` and retain the matching source identities.
arguments.stat: A compatible ggplot2 Stat or its name (default `"identity"`). Bound labels require the identity Stat and use the target’s post-Stat entities.
arguments.anchor_layer: [`auto_anchor()`](auto_anchor.html#api-auto_anchor) uses a unique compatible target. Select its ID if multiple layers are compatible. Use `NULL` for independent placement.
arguments.anchor: The general entry uses `"auto"`, which chooses the interval middle, the directional head for a primer or the residue anchor for a site or cut. Intervals can use `"start"`, `"end"`, `"middle"`, `"head"` and `"tail"`. Directional endpoints require reliable strand evidence.
arguments.position: Leave `NULL` for bound labels to follow the target placement, including strand side and lane. Independent labels can use the identity Position or [`position_offset()`](position_offset.html#api-position_offset).
arguments.label_layout: Use [`layout_label_fixed()`](layout_label_fixed.html#api-layout_label_fixed) to place text at a set offset, or [`layout_label_repel()`](layout_label_repel.html#api-layout_label_repel) to avoid collisions. The gene shortcut defaults to a horizontal fixed layout.
Named visual styles. Set `segment_colour`, `segment_linewidth` and `segment_linetype` for the leader. When omitted, the line colour follows the final text colour.
arguments.leader: Use `"auto"`, `"none"`, `"straight"` or `"elbow"` on the label layer. Both fixed and repelling layouts can draw an explicit leader.

geom_feature_label.roles: Map `label` to the source text. For a separate label subset, give the target layer ID and keep the matching `entity_id` or the appropriate `feature_id` or `site_id`. For independent labels, include the annotation location fields. Text aesthetics include `colour`, `size`, `family`, `fontface`, `angle` and `alpha`.
geom_feature_label.details: Labels follow an unambiguous source identity and its displayed feature, site or cut. Text placement and leaders preserve the underlying location. In circular maps outer labels default to bold unless you set or map `fontface`.

geom_link_ribbon.intro: Draw a ribbon between two source intervals with `geom_link_ribbon()`. Use `stat_link_bundle()` to combine nearby interval links or `stat_link_density()` to annotate links with two-axis density. The two statistical entry points draw the result as a ribbon. For two source points, see [`geom_link_line()`](geom_link_line.html#api-geom_link_line).

arguments.mapping: Aesthetic mapping from `aes()`. Local mappings take priority over matching inherited channels. To display computed values, map `after_stat(n_members)` for bundles or `after_stat(density)` for density.
arguments.data: Relationship table or a callback receiving the plot data. Provide one-based inclusive query and subject endpoints.
arguments.position: Defaults to `"identity"`. Use [`position_offset()`](position_offset.html#api-position_offset) for an explicit geometry offset.
arguments.stat: Explicit in `geom_link_ribbon()`. The default `"identity"` uses the supplied records. Use `"link_bundle"` or `"link_density"` to request the same statistics as the shortcuts.
arguments.geom: In the two statistical shortcuts, use their default and supported value `"link_ribbon"`.
arguments.bins: Controls the two endpoint grids for bundling and density. Use one positive number of bins for both axes or a named vector with `q` and `s`. The default is 80.
Named visual styles, route controls and geometry parameters. With `geom_link_ribbon(stat = ...)`, also pass the parameters of the selected statistic here.
arguments.na.rm: Defaults to `FALSE`. Set `TRUE` to omit records with missing endpoints or weights silently where supported. Invalid references, units and coordinates still raise errors.
arguments.show.legend: Defaults to `NA`. Use a logical value or named logical vector to control legend keys.
arguments.inherit.aes: Defaults to `TRUE`. Inherit plot mappings and evaluate them on the layer data.

geom_link_ribbon.roles: An interval link supplies `qaccver`, `qstart`, `qend`, `saccver`, `sstart` and `send`. Supply endpoint strands or direction where applicable. Map `fill`, `colour`, `alpha`, `linewidth` and `linetype` for ordinary ribbons, or endpoint fills with `fill_mode = "endpoint"`. The statistics accept `weight` (nonnegative, one per record by default) and `group`.
geom_link_ribbon.details: The equivalent bundle calls are `stat_link_bundle(bins = 20)` and `geom_link_ribbon(stat = "link_bundle", bins = 20)`. The bundle statistic groups links by the bins of their two midpoints, direction, reference pair and grouping. It draws the enclosing intervals and preserves source membership. The density statistic divides bin weight by the two-axis bin area and can additionally normalize density relative to each pair maximum. Its raw density describes midpoint concentration. Both statistics make computed columns available for mapping.

geom_track.intro: Draw source-position measurements or intervals in a track. Use `geom_track()` to select a geometry by name, or use a shortcut for points, lines, paths, steps, columns, counting bars, areas, tiles or full-band intervals.

arguments.mapping: Aesthetic mapping from `aes()`. Local mappings override matching inherited channels. Map `x` to a source location and `y` to a measurement or computed value when the geometry uses both. Full-band intervals use source endpoints.
arguments.data: A track table or a callback receiving plot-level data. Supply positions, observations or endpoints for the selected geometry and statistic.
arguments.geom: Explicit in `geom_track()`. Choose `"point"` (default), `"line"`, `"path"`, `"step"`, `"col"`, `"bar"`, `"area"`, `"tile"` or `"interval"`. Each shortcut selects its corresponding geometry.
arguments.stat: The general entry point uses `NULL` to choose the default for the geometry. Bars default to `"count"`; the other shortcuts default to `"identity"`. Supply a compatible Stat or supported name such as `"bin"`, `"summary"`, `"smooth"` or `"coverage"`. For coverage inputs and computed columns, see [`stat_coverage()`](stat_coverage.html#api-stat_coverage).
arguments.position: The general entry uses `NULL` to choose the default for the geometry. Columns, counting bars and areas default to `"stack"`; the others default to `"identity"`. A full-height interval with identity Stat requires identity Position.
arguments.track: Supply the ID of a declared track, or omit to create an individual band. Use add_track() for multiple layers in one band.
Styles and parameters for the selected geometry or Stat. Lines and paths support `closed` for a continuous complete circle; steps use `direction`. Columns, bars and areas accept `baseline`; areas also accept `outline`. Widths along the reference are in source units. Tile heights use the track’s numerical units. Use `measure` to name a numerical quantity and `bounds` to control errors or clipping outside the reference. A nonzero `baseline` requires identity Position. A parameter accepted by both an external Stat and the Geom must be disambiguated.
arguments.show.legend: Defaults to `NA`. Use a logical or named logical vector to control legend keys.
arguments.inherit.aes: Defaults to `TRUE`. Inherit plot mappings and evaluate them on the track data.

geom_track.roles: Use `accver` to identify the reference. Map `x` in source units and `y` in measurement units. A counting bar computes `after_stat(count)` and accepts an optional `weight` mapping. Interval layers use `start` and `end` and fill the physical band without training its numeric scale. Use `group` to distinguish series on the same reference. A [track band](layout_track.html#api-layout_track) controls physical space and [`scale_y_continuous()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/scale_continuous.html) controls the numerical scale.
geom_track.details:
Each standalone track layer creates a band with a stable automatic track ID. Supply the same named `track` to layers that share a band, or group them with `add_track()`. Use `layout_track()` to set physical placement.

On sequence-path coordinates a native `scale_y_*()` configures the latest band's numerical domain. Use `scale_for()` to select named track domains, with `by = "panel"` for per-facet training. Track X uses sequence positions. In Dotplot the native X and Y scales stay global. Ordinary visual scales train together by aesthetic.

layout_fusion.intro: Specify the panel positions of a Fusion composition. Use `layout_fusion()` for explicit rectangular bounds, including physical units, or `layout_fusion_grid()` for a matrix of panel names with relative row and column weights.
layout_fusion.roles: The rectangular table identifies panels with `panel` and supplies `xmin`, `xmax`, `ymin` and `ymax`. An optional `z` controls drawing order. A grid uses named cells, `NA` for empty cells and rectangles for panels spanning multiple cells.
layout_fusion.details: Both produce layout declarations for [`ggchord_fusion()`](ggchord_fusion.html#api-ggchord_fusion). An explicit grid is converted to relative rectangles. With `design = NULL`, the grid is generated from the composition’s panel names. Canvas placement leaves the source coordinates of each panel intact.

arguments.layout: A Fusion layout declaration from [`layout_fusion()`](layout_fusion.html#api-layout_fusion) or [`layout_fusion_grid()`](layout_fusion.html#api-layout_fusion_grid). The general constructor defaults to an automatic grid. The magnifier defaults to named `overview` and `detail` panels in one row, with relative widths 2 and 1.
arguments.guides: Defaults to `"keep"` in both entry points. Use `"collect"` to collect compatible guides.

ggchord_fusion.roles: The general constructor takes a named list of independent views. The magnifier takes its two views directly and a source region with `accver`, `start` and `end`. Use `...` on the magnifier for the supported zoom connector and highlight styles.
ggchord_fusion.details: Both return a Fusion composition. Layout and zoom marks operate on rendered views and preserve the underlying source data. To calculate statistics on a selected region, construct the detail plot with the desired data first.
